items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: Ray Wright asked me to write this piece... he came back to me and said your instincts are right and I’ll follow those indications... he was the perfect guy to get me going.

ctx.x: I’m wondering if in the time between “Elementals” and this piece, I would think your skill at orchestrating and arranging for a large ensemble has changed. Is that a fair statement?

Well I’ve learned a lot. I started with “Elementals” that was the first time. My brother informed me that he wasn’t going to do anymore orchestration for me and Ray Wright asked me to write this piece that we would do in Rochester at the Eastman School of Music. And I said I haven’t ever written anything for orchestra. And he said well I can hear in your music that your thinking is like a big orchestra. Well I had to agree with him because I do think sometimes with both hands full of notes.
I’m glad to hear you say that because sometimes when I listen to you play I feel like your two hands are like a big band.
